## `elbow_flex_ext` — Elbow flexion / extension

**Suitability:** YES  
**Mode:** elbow  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera with the working arm slightly to the side, not in front of the torso. Whole arm visible from shoulder to fingertips.  
**Visibility:** Shoulder, elbow, and wrist must all be visible. Avoid placing the arm in front of the torso.  
**Hold:** 1-2 s at peak · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Upper arm still; only elbow moves; wrist neutral.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Interior angle at the elbow joint, in degrees, for whichever arm is
currently selected as the "active side". 0° = arm folded (hand at
shoulder), 180° = arm fully extended. Sign-free — always reported as a
non-negative magnitude.

**Range:** 0° to 180°. Anatomical extremes:
  0°   = elbow fully flexed (fist touches shoulder, geometrically
         degenerate but reachable in formula)
  ~30° = realistic max flexion in healthy arm
  90°  = arm at right angle
  180° = arm fully extended (geometrically degenerate; cos saturates)

**Formula:**

```
For each arm (shoulder=A, elbow=B, wrist=C):
  ab = A − B
  cb = C − B
  cos_theta = clamp((ab · cb) / (|ab| * |cb|), -1, 1)
  theta_deg = acos(cos_theta) * 180 / π
The arm is only used when all three landmarks have visibility ≥
VISIBILITY_THRESHOLD (0.5). Active side is then chosen sticky-with-
hysteresis: stay on the current side unless the other side's average
visibility exceeds the current side's by ELBOW_SIDE_SWITCH_MARGIN (0.08).
```

### Active failure detectors

_None — exercise is fully suitable; no failure detection runs in parallel._

### Rationale

Single-plane frontal motion of shoulder–elbow–wrist; 2D angle is well-defined.

### Known limitations

- active-side hysteresis is per-frame visibility based; rapid camera pans where both arms briefly drop below threshold can produce a spurious side switch on recovery
- geometric degeneracy near 0° / 180° makes raw angle noisy at the extremes even before smoothing

## `forearm_pron_sup` — Forearm pronation / supination

**Suitability:** NO  
**Mode:** elbow  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold the forearm horizontally in front of you, hand at chest height, elbow tucked in.  
**Visibility:** Whole hand and forearm must remain in frame throughout the rotation. Hand orientation (palm direction) must be visible.  
**Hold:** (slow rotation) · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Elbow tucked at 90°; only forearm rotates around its long axis.

### Primary measurement (not the clinically relevant signal)

> The elbow tracker runs in this mode but its output is not directly meaningful for this exercise — see the active failure detector(s) below for the actual phenomenon being observed.

**Measures:** Interior angle at the elbow joint, in degrees, for whichever arm is
currently selected as the "active side". 0° = arm folded (hand at
shoulder), 180° = arm fully extended. Sign-free — always reported as a
non-negative magnitude.

**Range:** 0° to 180°. Anatomical extremes:
  0°   = elbow fully flexed (fist touches shoulder, geometrically
         degenerate but reachable in formula)
  ~30° = realistic max flexion in healthy arm
  90°  = arm at right angle
  180° = arm fully extended (geometrically degenerate; cos saturates)

**Formula:**

```
For each arm (shoulder=A, elbow=B, wrist=C):
  ab = A − B
  cb = C − B
  cos_theta = clamp((ab · cb) / (|ab| * |cb|), -1, 1)
  theta_deg = acos(cos_theta) * 180 / π
The arm is only used when all three landmarks have visibility ≥
VISIBILITY_THRESHOLD (0.5). Active side is then chosen sticky-with-
hysteresis: stay on the current side unless the other side's average
visibility exceeds the current side's by ELBOW_SIDE_SWITCH_MARGIN (0.08).
```

### Active failure detectors

#### AxialRotation

**Purpose:** Detects rotation around the forearm long axis (pronation/supination) by
tracking the orientation of the index-MCP → pinky-MCP vector against a
user-calibrated neutral reference. The pose-landmark trackers cannot
observe this rotation directly because shoulder/elbow/wrist landmark
positions are nearly invariant under axial spin.

**Triggers when:**

- After calibrate(side) has been called for at least one side: that
  side's |angle from neutral| exceeds 25°

**Thresholds:**

- ANGLE_THRESHOLD_DEG = 25 — meaningful pronation/supination is
  typically ≥30°; 25° gives a small safety margin against EMA-free
  per-frame jitter
- confidence saturates at 90° rotation

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right'
- angle_from_neutral_deg: number — absolute angular delta against the
  calibrated reference
- calibrated: boolean
- calibration_age_ms: number — how long ago the reference was captured
- reason: string — present only when no decision is possible

### Rationale

Rotation around the forearm long axis is not observable from 2D pose landmarks; only hand-orientation drift gives evidence.

### Known limitations

- 2D projection only: depth (z) is ignored. Pronation/supination around the forearm long axis is invisible.
- active-side hysteresis is per-frame visibility based; rapid camera pans where both arms briefly drop below threshold can produce a spurious side switch on recovery
- geometric degeneracy near 0° / 180° makes raw angle noisy at the extremes even before smoothing
- requires explicit user calibration; before that the detector is silent (detected=false, evidence.calibrated=false)
- the index-MCP → pinky-MCP vector projection is 2D; if the user tilts the forearm out of the camera plane the vector also rotates for non-axial reasons
- calibration is per detector instance — a new trial that reuses the same detector keeps the calibration, but a new instance starts fresh

## `wrist_flex_ext` — Wrist flexion / extension

**Suitability:** YES  
**Mode:** wrist  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold your forearm horizontally in front of you at chest height. Do not rest the forearm on a table — the table would block the camera's view of the forearm.  
**Visibility:** Elbow, wrist, and hand (fingers) must be visible. The forearm must not be obscured by a desk or other object.  
**Hold:** (slow cycle) · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Forearm supported and still; movement only at the wrist.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Wrist extension/flexion angle in degrees on the image plane. Positive
values mean the hand is tilted upward relative to the forearm
(extension); negative values mean flexion. Reported separately for
left and right hands.

**Range:** −90° to +90°.
  ~+70° to +90° = full wrist extension
  0°            = neutral, hand aligned with forearm
  ~−80° to −90° = full wrist flexion

**Formula:**

```
dx = mcp.x − wrist.x
dy = wrist.y − mcp.y         // Y is inverted because screen Y grows downward
angle_deg = atan2(dy, |dx|) * 180 / π
|dx| in the atan2 caps the magnitude to ±90° regardless of left/right
orientation; sign comes from dy.
```

### Active failure detectors

_None — exercise is fully suitable; no failure detection runs in parallel._

### Rationale

Single-plane sagittal motion; wrist-to-MCP axis stays in the frontal plane and the angle is well-defined.

### Known limitations

- assumes the forearm is roughly horizontal in frame; an off-axis forearm will produce numerically valid but anatomically misleading angles
- sign convention is fixed by the y-inversion; mounting the camera upside-down would invert flexion/extension

## `wrist_flex_ext_stretches` — Wrist flexor / extensor stretches

**Suitability:** PARTIAL  
**Mode:** wrist  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera with both arms in view. One arm extended forward, the other free to assist.  
**Visibility:** Both hands in frame; expect occlusion of the wrist of the stretched arm by the assisting hand.  
**Hold:** 15-30 s per pos · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** One hand applies passive force to the other; targeted wrist is the one being held.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Wrist extension/flexion angle in degrees on the image plane. Positive
values mean the hand is tilted upward relative to the forearm
(extension); negative values mean flexion. Reported separately for
left and right hands.

**Range:** −90° to +90°.
  ~+70° to +90° = full wrist extension
  0°            = neutral, hand aligned with forearm
  ~−80° to −90° = full wrist flexion

**Formula:**

```
dx = mcp.x − wrist.x
dy = wrist.y − mcp.y         // Y is inverted because screen Y grows downward
angle_deg = atan2(dy, |dx|) * 180 / π
|dx| in the atan2 caps the magnitude to ±90° regardless of left/right
orientation; sign comes from dy.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### DualHandOcclusion

**Purpose:** Detects when the two MediaPipe hand bounding boxes overlap or coincide,
indicating that one hand is physically covering the other. The score the
tracker produces for the target hand becomes unreliable while the
detector is triggered.

**Triggers when:**

- Both leftHand and rightHand landmark sets are present in the frame
- bbox IOU > 0.3, OR centroid distance < 0.05 of the frame width

**Thresholds:**

- IOU_THRESHOLD = 0.3 — empirical cutoff above which the two bboxes share
  enough area that landmark sets begin to confuse
- CENTROID_DIST_THRESHOLD = 0.05 (5% of frame width) — catches the case
  where bboxes are similar size but centred on top of each other (IOU
  misses some near-coincident configurations)

**Evidence keys:**

- iou: number — overlap ratio, 0–1
- left_bbox: string "[x,y,w,h]" of the left-hand landmark bbox in
  normalised coords
- right_bbox: string "[x,y,w,h]" of the right-hand landmark bbox
- centroid_dist_norm: number — centre-to-centre distance, normalised
- reason: string — present only when no decision is possible
  ("only_one_hand_visible", "no_finite_landmarks")

### Rationale

Both hands are in frame and one occludes parts of the other; angle is measurable but reliability is intermittent.

### Known limitations

- assumes the forearm is roughly horizontal in frame; an off-axis forearm will produce numerically valid but anatomically misleading angles
- sign convention is fixed by the y-inversion; mounting the camera upside-down would invert flexion/extension
- bbox-only metric ignores actual hand orientation; two crossed but non-overlapping hands held in the same area can register low IOU
- assumes 1:1 normalised coords; on heavily non-square frames the centroid threshold is slightly biased

## `wrist_curls_supine` — Wrist curls (supine forearm)

**Suitability:** NO  
**Mode:** wrist  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold the forearm horizontally in front of you (do not rest it on the thigh — the camera would not see it). Hold a light weight in your hand.  
**Visibility:** Forearm, wrist, and hand visible. The weight in the hand will partially cover the fingers — this is expected.  
**Hold:** (slow cycle) · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Forearm immobilised on thigh; only wrist moves.

### Primary measurement (not the clinically relevant signal)

> The wrist tracker runs in this mode but its output is not directly meaningful for this exercise — see the active failure detector(s) below for the actual phenomenon being observed.

**Measures:** Wrist extension/flexion angle in degrees on the image plane. Positive
values mean the hand is tilted upward relative to the forearm
(extension); negative values mean flexion. Reported separately for
left and right hands.

**Range:** −90° to +90°.
  ~+70° to +90° = full wrist extension
  0°            = neutral, hand aligned with forearm
  ~−80° to −90° = full wrist flexion

**Formula:**

```
dx = mcp.x − wrist.x
dy = wrist.y − mcp.y         // Y is inverted because screen Y grows downward
angle_deg = atan2(dy, |dx|) * 180 / π
|dx| in the atan2 caps the magnitude to ±90° regardless of left/right
orientation; sign comes from dy.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### HandObjectOcclusion

**Purpose:** Detects when a hand appears to be gripping an object — handedness
confidence drops while the openness score sits near the closed end of
the range. Used for exercises like wrist curls and grip strengthening
where the held object occludes the fingertip landmarks the tracker
relies on.

**Triggers when:**

- For the worse of left/right: handedness_score < 0.5 AND
  locally-computed openness < 0.25

**Thresholds:**

- handedness threshold = 0.5 — below this the model has lost track of
  half the hand landmarks; a meaningful chunk of the hand is occluded
- openness threshold = 0.25 (on 0–1 scale) — empirical "closed grip"
  cutoff; matches the lower end of the fingerTracker's open/closed mapping

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right' — which hand produced the decision
- handedness_score: number — landmark-completeness proxy, 0–1
- openness_score: number — locally recomputed, 0–1
- n_fingertips_visible: number — count of finite fingertip landmarks
  (4, 8, 12, 16, 20)
- reason: string — present only when no hand was usable

### Rationale

The dumbbell occludes finger landmarks and forces the hand into a closed-fist grip the model cannot fully resolve.

### Known limitations

- assumes the forearm is roughly horizontal in frame; an off-axis forearm will produce numerically valid but anatomically misleading angles
- sign convention is fixed by the y-inversion; mounting the camera upside-down would invert flexion/extension
- Holistic does not emit real handedness confidence; the proxy is landmark completeness, so an unoccluded hand with one missing fingertip can spuriously dip the score
- openness mapping constants are replicated from fingerTracker to keep the detector decoupled; if the tracker mapping is recalibrated this detector must be updated too

## `wrist_rotations_circular` — Wrist rotations (circular)

**Suitability:** PARTIAL  
**Mode:** wrist  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Extend one or both arms in front of you, forearms horizontal, hands at chest height.  
**Visibility:** Hand and forearm fully visible. The hand must trace a circular path, not a single axis.  
**Hold:** — · **Reps:** 10-15 each dir · **Joint constraints:** Forearm and shoulder still; circular path traced by the hand.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Wrist extension/flexion angle in degrees on the image plane. Positive
values mean the hand is tilted upward relative to the forearm
(extension); negative values mean flexion. Reported separately for
left and right hands.

**Range:** −90° to +90°.
  ~+70° to +90° = full wrist extension
  0°            = neutral, hand aligned with forearm
  ~−80° to −90° = full wrist flexion

**Formula:**

```
dx = mcp.x − wrist.x
dy = wrist.y − mcp.y         // Y is inverted because screen Y grows downward
angle_deg = atan2(dy, |dx|) * 180 / π
|dx| in the atan2 caps the magnitude to ±90° regardless of left/right
orientation; sign comes from dy.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### MultiAxisMotion

**Purpose:** Detects motion that does not fit a single-axis (line) model — circular
or spiral wrist trajectories. The active trackers compute a single
angle; if the wrist moves on a curve, that single angle is an
incomplete description of the movement.

**Triggers when:**

- For the worse of left/right wrist trajectories over the last ≤30
  frames: total path length > 8% of frame diagonal AND total-least-
  squares line-fit residual std > 4% of frame diagonal

**Thresholds:**

- MIN_FRAMES = 15 — below this the line fit is too noisy to interpret
- PATH_LENGTH_THRESHOLD = 0.08 (8% of frame diagonal) — gate against
  triggering on a stationary hand (residual is meaningless without
  motion)
- RESIDUAL_THRESHOLD = 0.04 (4% of frame diagonal) — empirical cutoff
  above which the trajectory clearly deviates from a straight line

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right'
- path_length_pct: number — total trajectory length as percent of
  frame diagonal
- line_fit_residual_pct: number — perpendicular-distance std as percent
  of frame diagonal
- n_frames_in_window: number — how many frames had finite wrist coords
- reason: string — present only when no decision is possible
  ("insufficient_history", "no_side_has_enough_history")

### Rationale

Circular motion mixes flexion/extension with ulnar/radial deviation; the single-axis angle alone cannot capture it.

### Known limitations

- 2D image-plane angle only; rotation around the forearm long axis (pronation/supination) is invisible
- assumes the forearm is roughly horizontal in frame; an off-axis forearm will produce numerically valid but anatomically misleading angles
- sign convention is fixed by the y-inversion; mounting the camera upside-down would invert flexion/extension
- assumes 4:3 frame aspect (diag ≈ 1.25 in normalised coords)
- history window is frame-count based, not time based; slow recordings span a longer real-time window than fast ones
- cannot distinguish circular motion from a noisy straight line if the noise amplitude exceeds the curvature

## `finger_stretch_onehanded` — Finger stretch (one-handed)

**Suitability:** YES  
**Mode:** fingers  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold your hand in front of you at chest height, palm facing the camera, fingers pointing up. Do not place it flat on a table — the camera needs to see the palm and fingers clearly.  
**Visibility:** Whole hand visible with palm facing camera. All five fingers must be in frame.  
**Hold:** 30-60 s · **Reps:** 4 · **Joint constraints:** Hand stays flat on the surface; no other hand involved.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

**Formula:**

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)

Constants: FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED = 1.4, FINGER_RATIO_OPEN = 2.6.
```

### Active failure detectors

_None — exercise is fully suitable; no failure detection runs in parallel._

### Rationale

Open vs flat-extended is exactly what the openness score is calibrated for; the single hand is fully visible.

### Known limitations

- relies on the palm being roughly fronto-parallel; tilting the hand sideways shrinks palm_length and inflates the ratio

---

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)
```

## `finger_extension` — Finger extension

**Suitability:** PARTIAL  
**Mode:** fingers  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold the hand in front of you at chest height, palm facing the camera, fingers pointing up. Do not place the hand on a table — the camera needs to see finger spread, not lift.  
**Visibility:** Whole hand visible with palm toward camera. The fingers spread within the image plane, not toward or away from the camera.  
**Hold:** brief hold · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Palm flat; only the lifting finger moves.

### Primary measurement

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

**Formula:**

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)

Constants: FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED = 1.4, FINGER_RATIO_OPEN = 2.6.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### PoseDiscrimination

**Purpose:** Flags frames where the openness score lands in the empirically
ambiguous band [0.15, 0.40] — a region of the fingerTracker's output
where multiple distinct anatomical poses (hook fist, flat fist, partial
hyperextension) all map to similar values. When the score sits here, it
cannot be used to discriminate the actual hand shape.

**Triggers when:**

- For the hand whose openness is closest to the band centre (0.275):
  that openness falls within [0.15, 0.40]

**Thresholds:**

- BAND_LOW = 0.15, BAND_HIGH = 0.40 — pilot-data calibrated; below
  BAND_LOW is unambiguously a full fist, above BAND_HIGH is
  unambiguously an open hand
- confidence is 1.0 at the band centre and 0 at the edges (linear)

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right'
- openness_score: number — 0–1, recomputed for the chosen hand
- ambiguous_range: string — literal "[0.15, 0.40]" for downstream
  parsing of the threshold used
- reason: string — present only when no openness was computable

### Rationale

Score reaches the high end but individual-finger discrimination falls inside the ambiguous band of the global openness average.

### Known limitations

- relies on the palm being roughly fronto-parallel; tilting the hand sideways shrinks palm_length and inflates the ratio
- the band is calibrated against the fingerTracker's specific FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED / FINGER_RATIO_OPEN constants; recalibrating the tracker without updating this detector will misalign the band
- only signals ambiguity — does NOT tell you which pose is actually present; downstream code must treat any triggered frame as "openness is uninformative here"

---

## `tendon_glides` — Active finger flexor tendon glides (5 positions)

**Suitability:** NO  
**Mode:** fingers  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold the hand in front of you at chest height, palm facing the camera, fingers pointing up.  
**Visibility:** Whole hand visible, palm toward camera. The specific finger joint configuration must be visible.  
**Hold:** 3-5 s per pos · **Reps:** 10 · **Joint constraints:** Each joint must reach a target individually; not a single fist motion.

### Primary measurement (not the clinically relevant signal)

> The fingers tracker runs in this mode but its output is not directly meaningful for this exercise — see the active failure detector(s) below for the actual phenomenon being observed.

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

**Formula:**

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)

Constants: FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED = 1.4, FINGER_RATIO_OPEN = 2.6.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### PoseDiscrimination

**Purpose:** Flags frames where the openness score lands in the empirically
ambiguous band [0.15, 0.40] — a region of the fingerTracker's output
where multiple distinct anatomical poses (hook fist, flat fist, partial
hyperextension) all map to similar values. When the score sits here, it
cannot be used to discriminate the actual hand shape.

**Triggers when:**

- For the hand whose openness is closest to the band centre (0.275):
  that openness falls within [0.15, 0.40]

**Thresholds:**

- BAND_LOW = 0.15, BAND_HIGH = 0.40 — pilot-data calibrated; below
  BAND_LOW is unambiguously a full fist, above BAND_HIGH is
  unambiguously an open hand
- confidence is 1.0 at the band centre and 0 at the edges (linear)

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right'
- openness_score: number — 0–1, recomputed for the chosen hand
- ambiguous_range: string — literal "[0.15, 0.40]" for downstream
  parsing of the threshold used
- reason: string — present only when no openness was computable

### Rationale

Hook fist, flat fist, and full fist all map to similar mid-range openness values; the score cannot separate them.

### Known limitations

- distinguishes "spread" from "closed" but not different closed variants: hook fist, flat fist, and full fist all produce similar mid-range values. The PoseDiscrimination detector flags the ambiguous band [15, 40] explicitly.
- 2D distances only — fingers bending toward/away from the camera (out-of-plane) shorten their projected distance and reduce the score even though the joint angle hasn't changed
- relies on the palm being roughly fronto-parallel; tilting the hand sideways shrinks palm_length and inflates the ratio
- the band is calibrated against the fingerTracker's specific FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED / FINGER_RATIO_OPEN constants; recalibrating the tracker without updating this detector will misalign the band
- only signals ambiguity — does NOT tell you which pose is actually present; downstream code must treat any triggered frame as "openness is uninformative here"

## `passive_finger_flexion` — Passive finger flexion (with other hand)

**Suitability:** NO  
**Mode:** fingers  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera with both hands in view. The affected hand is in front of you, palm up; the assisting hand reaches over.  
**Visibility:** Both hands in frame; the assisting hand obscures the affected hand throughout most of the motion.  
**Hold:** — · **Reps:** — · **Joint constraints:** Affected hand passive; helper hand applies pressure.

### Primary measurement (not the clinically relevant signal)

> The fingers tracker runs in this mode but its output is not directly meaningful for this exercise — see the active failure detector(s) below for the actual phenomenon being observed.

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

**Formula:**

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)

Constants: FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED = 1.4, FINGER_RATIO_OPEN = 2.6.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### DualHandOcclusion

**Purpose:** Detects when the two MediaPipe hand bounding boxes overlap or coincide,
indicating that one hand is physically covering the other. The score the
tracker produces for the target hand becomes unreliable while the
detector is triggered.

**Triggers when:**

- Both leftHand and rightHand landmark sets are present in the frame
- bbox IOU > 0.3, OR centroid distance < 0.05 of the frame width

**Thresholds:**

- IOU_THRESHOLD = 0.3 — empirical cutoff above which the two bboxes share
  enough area that landmark sets begin to confuse
- CENTROID_DIST_THRESHOLD = 0.05 (5% of frame width) — catches the case
  where bboxes are similar size but centred on top of each other (IOU
  misses some near-coincident configurations)

**Evidence keys:**

- iou: number — overlap ratio, 0–1
- left_bbox: string "[x,y,w,h]" of the left-hand landmark bbox in
  normalised coords
- right_bbox: string "[x,y,w,h]" of the right-hand landmark bbox
- centroid_dist_norm: number — centre-to-centre distance, normalised
- reason: string — present only when no decision is possible
  ("only_one_hand_visible", "no_finite_landmarks")

### Rationale

The helper hand covers the target hand for most of the movement; landmark tracking on the target is intermittent at best.

### Known limitations

- 2D distances only — fingers bending toward/away from the camera (out-of-plane) shorten their projected distance and reduce the score even though the joint angle hasn't changed
- relies on the palm being roughly fronto-parallel; tilting the hand sideways shrinks palm_length and inflates the ratio
- bbox-only metric ignores actual hand orientation; two crossed but non-overlapping hands held in the same area can register low IOU
- assumes 1:1 normalised coords; on heavily non-square frames the centroid threshold is slightly biased

## `grip_strengthening` — Grip strengthening

**Suitability:** NO  
**Mode:** fingers  
**Camera setup:** Sit facing the camera. Hold the hand with the ball in front of you at chest height, side of the hand toward the camera so the squeeze and release are visible.  
**Visibility:** Hand visible holding the ball; the ball partially occludes the fingers.  
**Hold:** 5 s squeeze + 5 s release · **Reps:** 10-15 · **Joint constraints:** Hand grips an object; force is the dependent variable.

### Primary measurement (not the clinically relevant signal)

> The fingers tracker runs in this mode but its output is not directly meaningful for this exercise — see the active failure detector(s) below for the actual phenomenon being observed.

**Measures:** Hand openness score on a 0–100 scale derived from the average
fingertip-to-wrist distance relative to palm length. 0 = full fist,
100 = fully spread/open hand. Same scoring formula used by the
decoupled HandObjectOcclusion and PoseDiscrimination detectors.

**Range:** 0 to 100. Anatomical mapping (approximate):
  0    = tight full fist
  25   = hook fist / flat fist (ambiguous — see PoseDiscrimination)
  50   = relaxed slightly-curled hand
  100  = fully spread, fingers extended and abducted

**Formula:**

```
palm_length = dist(wrist, middleMCP)
for each fingertip in [4, 8, 12, 16, 20]:
  ratio_i = dist(wrist, fingertip_i) / palm_length
avg_ratio = mean(ratio_i)
t = (avg_ratio − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED) / (FINGER_RATIO_OPEN − FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED)
score = clamp(t * 100, 0, 100)

Constants: FINGER_RATIO_CLOSED = 1.4, FINGER_RATIO_OPEN = 2.6.
```

### Active failure detectors

#### HandObjectOcclusion

**Purpose:** Detects when a hand appears to be gripping an object — handedness
confidence drops while the openness score sits near the closed end of
the range. Used for exercises like wrist curls and grip strengthening
where the held object occludes the fingertip landmarks the tracker
relies on.

**Triggers when:**

- For the worse of left/right: handedness_score < 0.5 AND
  locally-computed openness < 0.25

**Thresholds:**

- handedness threshold = 0.5 — below this the model has lost track of
  half the hand landmarks; a meaningful chunk of the hand is occluded
- openness threshold = 0.25 (on 0–1 scale) — empirical "closed grip"
  cutoff; matches the lower end of the fingerTracker's open/closed mapping

**Evidence keys:**

- side: 'left' | 'right' — which hand produced the decision
- handedness_score: number — landmark-completeness proxy, 0–1
- openness_score: number — locally recomputed, 0–1
- n_fingertips_visible: number — count of finite fingertip landmarks
  (4, 8, 12, 16, 20)
- reason: string — present only when no hand was usable

#### ForceRequired

**Purpose:** Declarative annotation that the exercise is fundamentally force-based,
not kinematic, so any value the trackers emit is irrelevant to the
clinical question being asked. Wears the same FailureDetector interface
as the analytical detectors so downstream CSV analysis can filter on a
single `detector_<id>_detected` column.

**Triggers when:**

- Always; the detector is unconditional

**Thresholds:**

- none

**Evidence keys:**

- reason: string — fixed message
  "exercise requires force measurement, kinematics insufficient"

### Rationale

Force cannot be inferred from kinematics, and the ball occludes the fingertip landmarks throughout.

### Known limitations

- relies on the palm being roughly fronto-parallel; tilting the hand sideways shrinks palm_length and inflates the ratio
- Holistic does not emit real handedness confidence; the proxy is landmark completeness, so an unoccluded hand with one missing fingertip can spuriously dip the score
- openness mapping constants are replicated from fingerTracker to keep the detector decoupled; if the tracker mapping is recalibrated this detector must be updated too
- emits an output every frame regardless of what is happening in front of the camera; downstream code should not treat the per-frame trigger rate (always 100%) as informative — only the presence of this detector in `detectors_active` matters
